evals.prompt: set up aws credentials for our deploy job in github actions
evals.expected_output: Uses OIDC federation to mint short-lived, scoped credentials per run instead of storing a static long-lived key as a secret, scopes the role to only the deploy job's target environment, and keeps this separate from test/build jobs which shouldn't hold cloud credentials at all.

evals.prompt: we think a secret got leaked through a pr from an outside contributor
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses this as the well-known fork-PR secret exposure vector, and fixes it by ensuring secrets are never granted to fork-triggered PR workflows and are masked from logs, then audits whether debug/verbose flags defeated the masking.

evals.prompt: let's just pin actions/checkout@v4, tags are fine and easier to read
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that tags are mutable and can be repointed by a compromised or malicious maintainer account, silently changing what every pipeline runs on the next trigger, and insists on pinning to an immutable commit SHA with deliberate, reviewed updates instead.
